_comment: CI-only signing key. Generated once by the workflow with keytool, then committed
so that every future build has the SAME signature - otherwise each run would produce
a different one and installed extensions could no longer be updated.
Its private key and password are deliberately public: the fingerprint declared in
repo/repo.json is already an Android debug certificate, so this does not weaken the
trust model, and it means nothing can be lost or rotated by accident.
To use a private key instead, set the SIGNING_KEY (base64 of a .jks), ALIAS,
KEY_STORE_PASSWORD and KEY_PASSWORD repository secrets; they take precedence.
An APK is only published if every gate passes. Tachimanga runs the classic
Mihon/Tachiyomi extension API; extensions compiled against keiyoushi extensions-lib
1.6 (KeiSource) require Mihon 0.20.1+ and fail on Tachimanga.
These are checked on the built APK, so they cannot be fooled by build-config changes.
Tachimanga requires minSdk 21 (that is what its 'Unsupported extension' message
tells you to rebuild with). Upstream raised minSdk to 26 in gradle/kei.versions.toml,
which would make every extension below unloadable, so builds rewrite that value to
this number first, and the gate still rejects anything that ends up above it.

extensions._comment: Upstream moved to libVersion 1.6 / KeiSource on 2026-09-11, so this is pinned to the last revision that still uses the classic API, with the ?verify= image-parsing fix backported onto it.

_comment: Checked on every run without building anything, to give early warning that a module
changed in a way that affects us: migrated to the incompatible API, moved to a newer
classic revision we could pick up, or disappeared (upstream removes dead sites).
